A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework, renamed from TAGExplainer to GraphNarrator. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, component ablations, Expert Iteration trajectories, distillation comparisons, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds human evaluations of generated explanations and training pseudo-labels, plus a saliency ablation.

M1.justification: The main pipeline and three optimization objectives remain. Section 4.1 adds pruning of nodes lacking tokens above a saliency threshold. Section 4.3 changes the stated distillation-data source from candidates generated after teacher training to candidates accumulated during Expert Iteration. These are limited procedural revisions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate explanations on Cora, DBLP, and Book-History, with identical dataset statistics and classification tasks. The new human evaluations concern these same domains. Molecular graphs appear as introductory motivation in v2, without corresponding experiments.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains LLaMA3.1 8B, GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4o, and GPT-4o-based SMV. Comparator membership changes in the ablation comparison: v1 Table 2 includes w/o Expert Iteration, whereas v2 Table 3 replaces that variant with w/o saliency.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a human-evaluation protocol using three annotators with computational-linguistics knowledge, 50 examples per dataset and method, and 1–7 ratings for understandability, decision-process insight, semantic information, and structural information. Appendix C applies this evaluation to pseudo-labels. The existing automatic metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a human assessment of pseudo-label quality and a saliency-removal ablation, while removing the explicit Expert-Iteration-removal result. The three objective ablations, candidate-selection analyses, distillation comparison, and qualitative cases are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The new human evaluations report point ratings without uncertainty estimates or inter-annotator agreement analysis.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantive human-evaluation results in Tables 2 and 4; for example, DBLP structural informativeness is 5.4 for GraphNarrator versus 3.6 for GPT-4o in Table 2. It also adds w/o saliency results and removes w/o Expert Iteration results. The main automatic scores, distillation scores, and plotted training trends remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The graph formulation, PMI objectives, threshold averaging, and explanation-length ratio retain their mathematical substance. Appendix B adds the standard tokenwise factorization of conditional probability to explain score computation, without introducing a new theoretical result, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The central pseudo-label, Expert Iteration, and distillation contributions remain. v2 broadens the abstract and introduction's novelty framing from explanations for TAG-learning models to explanations for GNNs, and adds a human-preference claim. Its formal problem and conclusion remain TAG-focused.

C2.justification: v2 attributes smaller improvements on Cora to OCR-related data quality and discusses human ratings in terms of information preservation and the LLM backbone. It adds an explicit computational limitation: inference on extremely large subgraphs can exceed two minutes. The existing interpretation of trade-offs among the three objectives remains.

D1.justification: v2 resolves important implementation omissions by specifying the explained model as bert-base-uncased plus two-layer GraphSAGE, with learning rate 0.001 and batch size 500. Appendix B explains serialization and probability extraction; Appendix F adds hardware, runtime, API cost, and iteration counts. These disclosures do not establish that the retained experiments changed settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to GRAG, ELAD, and Liu et al.'s self-explanation work, while removing STaR and several TAG-learning references. It condenses the related-work discussion and broadens the introductory GNN positioning, while retaining the central distinction from saliency-based and LLM-generated explanations.

P1.justification: v2 renames the framework and title, substantially rewrites the introduction, removes the contribution list, and condenses related work and method exposition. It reorganizes the experimental narrative, moves qualitative evaluation into Appendix A, restructures the appendices, and shortens the printed prompt examples.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. v2 redraws the introductory and framework diagrams, separates verbalization into Figure 3, adds serialization and masking illustrations, and converts the main training plots from bars to lines. Human-evaluation tables are added, existing displays are relocated, and boxed prompts become ordinary appendix text.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's automatic metrics and qualitative cases, v2 provides direct human evaluations and important target-model, scoring, and computational details, improving empirical support and reproducibility. These gains are tempered by removal of the explicit Expert Iteration control, stale ablation prose, and reversed GPT-4o Cora structural/semantic ratings between Tables 2 and 4. The net improvement is useful but limited.
